prayerExcerpt.en-US: Can we call to mind the fervor of the Saints in laboring and suffering cheerfully for God, and not feel a holy ardor glow in our own breasts, and our souls strongly affected with their heroic sentiments of virtue?
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Poderemos recordar o fervor dos Santos em trabalhar e sofrer alegremente por Deus, e não sentir um santo ardor abrasar nossos próprios peitos, e nossas almas fortemente comovidas por seus heroicos sentimentos de virtude?

meta.face: An Egyptian of Alexandria of about forty with a warm, deep-bronze complexion and a LEAN, ANGULAR face with a strong, SQUARE jaw — a straight, fairly narrow forehead, HIGH, SHARP cheekbones over HOLLOW cheeks, a LONG, straight nose with a slightly flared base, deep-set, dark eyes under THICK, straight black brows, FULL lips, a square chin; thick, tightly CURLED black hair cropped short; a SHORT, CLOSE-TRIMMED, curly black beard along the jaw; the look calm and unashamed. Not peter_alexandria (round, full, grey, short-nosed), the old desert monks macarius_alexandria, pachomius (long, bald), john_egypt and paphnutius, the round, fleshy severianus_scythopolis, the bald, domed eulogius_alexandria or the veteran Tarachus of tarachus_companions (square, broken-nosed).
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The one image on English Wikipedia, Spinello Aretino's 'Saint Nemesius and Saint John the Baptist' (1385, Budapest; `consult/batch-41/commons-Nemesion.txt`), is a late Tuscan altarpiece figure and is not followed. The face is typed from the book ('an Egyptian', of Alexandria) and the tunic is an Alexandrian's of the third century; the calm follows the book's account of his clearing himself of theft and going to the fire for Christ. The fire, the thieves and his companions are left off.
